pr_title: Ensure that default values for platform-based flags are applied.

issue_context.title: Platform-based flags cannot reset Starlark flags to the default value
issue_context.body:
(Original title: "A 'cursed' label flag")

Every Starlark flag has a default value defined when it is declared. If a different value is set, platform-based flags should be able to explicitly set the default and have that override the previous value, but currently they are ignored.

See https://github.com/katre/bazel/commit/2aa5c32c9390160f9ea62a796de06a00786be565 for a small demo.

# Original description

### Description of the bug:


I found a truly bizarre bug that I can't make heads or tails of. If a custom host platform explicitly sets a _particular label flag in Pigweed_ to a value, and a platform set via `platform_data` attempts to override it, then the override will fail.

What's bizarre about it is that,

1. It only happens when the target platform is set via `platform_data`, not if it's set on the command line.
2. I've not been able to reproduce this with a minimal upstream repository, only with Pigweed itself.
3. In fact I've not been able to reproduce it with other label flags in Pigweed, including label flags defined in the same `BUILD.bazel` file. As far as I can tell, there's only one unlucky flag that cannot be overridden!

@katre I know you have a lot on your plate, but if you have any suggestions for how to debug this, they'd be very appreciated. This one is a real head-scratcher, and also prevented me from deploying platform-based flags.

### Which category does this issue belong to?

Configurability

### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


https://github.com/tpudlik/cursed_flag

### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


release 8.0.0-pre.20240618.2

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


_No response_

### If this is a regression, please try to identify the Bazel commit where the bug was introduced with bazelisk --bisect.


_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

_No response_

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

_No response_
comments:
Looks like your [device platform is setting the `label_flag` back to the default](https://github.com/tpudlik/cursed_flag/blob/main/BUILD.bazel#L24): is that also what you're doing with the other flag you tested (`@pigweed//pw_system:device_handler_backend`)?

I wonder if there's something that says "oh, this is the default, so it's not set"? I'll also try debugging, but if you can test that case it'd be handy.

A better way to cquery for these things is to use `filter` and `deps`:

```
$ bazel-dev cquery --implicit_deps --tool_deps -- 'filter("@pigweed//pw_system:", deps(//:binary_for_device)'
```

This shows all the deps in `@pigweed//pw_system`, so you can see whether it's the one you want, rather than probing via `somepath`. The one restriction is that you need `--implicit_deps --tool_deps` to make sure nothing is filtered out.

> Looks like your [device platform is setting the label_flag back to the default](https://github.com/tpudlik/cursed_flag/blob/main/BUILD.bazel#L24): is that also what you're doing with the other flag you tested (`@pigweed//pw_system:device_handler_backend`)?

[Indeed it's not!](https://cs.opensource.google/pigweed/pigweed/+/main:pw_system/BUILD.bazel;l=193-213;drc=a158415a5c07e71b95aeec5411ffe5da215a0b1a) And if I fix that, i.e. do,

```
$ sed -i 's/pw_system:io_backend/pw_system:device_handler_backend/g' BUILD.bazel
$ sed -i 's/pw_system:sys_io_target_io/pw_system:unknown_device_handler/g' BUILD.bazel
```

I reproduce the bug with this flag, too. (I had to add `build --@rules_python//python/config_settings:exec_tools_toolchain=enabled` to the `.bazelrc` and `rules_python` 0.34.0 to `MODULE.bazel` to avoid some unrelated build failures.) So it _is_ something about setting the flag back to its default.
Good to know, that should help narrow it down.
Okay, I have a very minimal test that shows the same problem, so now I can debug and fix that. I'm going to update the issue name and description to clarify the problem.

Ah, that's great. I _tried_ to produce such a minimal test (having the host platform set the flag to default and the target platform override it), but couldn't get it to work. That is, my minimal repro didn't actually reproduce the bug, everything worked as intended.
@tpudlik Can you build bazel from https://github.com/katre/bazel/tree/i23147-cursed-flag-fix and let me know if it addresses your reproduction?
Yes, I verified that Bazel built from that branch doesn't exhibit the bug, either in my minimal example or in the larger project that originally motivated it. Thank you!
Excellent, I'll clean it up a bit and get it merged.

Okay, got more involved after @gregestren's comment (https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/23159#discussion_r1697576017).

Sending out a bunch of changes (unfortunately internally, not in GH), hopefully will address this properly.

review_comments:
I need some walkthrough here.

As background, we expect any BuildOptions with a Starlark value set to its default won't have that entry at all in `BuildOptions.getStarlarkOptions()`. That protects against unnecessary forking of configurations that are conceptually equivalent. Does this change any of that, or is that unrelated?

I didn't realize we even had `includeDefaultValues` in `StarlarkOptionsParser` and found it was added specifically for `canonicalize-flags` at https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/33e9bf119550950ebcf0ffb2c7b372c17748dd7d. That logic, I think, wasn't meant to trigger in `bazel build`.

> Every Starlark flag has a default value defined when it is declared. If a different value is set, platform-based flags should be able to explicitly set the default and have that override the previous value, but currently they are ignored.

That makes sense. How does this code trigger that? I realize this happens in `ParsedFlagsFunction` which creates a custom `StarlarkOptionsParser` that passes that. That produces a list of flags that we need to apply to platform mapping? Then does `PlatformFlagsProducer` ensure those flags are set but *also* ensure default-set Starlark flags aren't present in the ultimate `BuildOptions` that powers the configuration?

I think I understand the bug though. The code as is doesn't even register flags being set to their defaults as something that needs to be changed, since the custom `StarlarkOptionsParser` just drops them?

This is a good point: the code at present leaves the defaults for Starlark flags in the build options.

I think what is needed is for `ParsedFlagsFunction` to indicate that some flags get set to a specific value, and that some are removed entirely. I'm not sure how to model that: possibly with an `Optional`?

> I think I understand the bug though. The code as is doesn't even register flags being set to their defaults as something that needs to be changed, since the custom StarlarkOptionsParser just drops them?

Correct, before this change, if the platform says `--//starlark:flag=default`, it just isn't present in the list of flags. So something needs to signal "this flag needs to be explicitly removed".

I'm curious what @aranguyen makes of this since I think scoped transitions will have similar issues.

Which code uses the results of `PlatformFlagsProducer` to produce the final `BuildOptions` that feed the configuration?  Is that somewhere in `BuildConfigurationKeyProducer`?
